current_qualitative.3m: Core moat is rooted in a massive global installed base of distributed control systems (DeltaV, Ovation) and mission-critical measurement instrumentation (Rosemount, Micro Motion, Fisher valves) embedded in continuous process facilities (chemical, refining, power, life sciences). Switching costs are near-prohibitive due to severe operational disruption risk, 24/7 continuous process downtime costs, and strict regulatory requalification burdens. Historical 10-year median ROIC of 14.2% and gross margins >42-45% demonstrate pricing power, but returns on total invested capital have been diluted by heavy acquisition goodwill (AspenTech, NI). Erosion threats include open process automation (OPAF) standards and IT/OT convergence.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Emerson commands an entrenched installed base in process automation (DeltaV, Fisher, Rosemount), it operates in Tier 3 Capital Goods (baseline CAP 10-15 years) and faces severe structural headwinds under the 5-Macrotrend framework. A significant portion of its process automation revenue remains anchored to fossil fuel refining, chemicals, and hydrocarbon infrastructure facing long-term energy transition headwinds (Macrotrend 4). Simultaneously, the ongoing transition toward open-architecture, software-defined automation (Macrotrend 1) challenges proprietary hardware lock-in, forcing multi-billion dollar defensive M&A (AspenTech, National Instruments) at full valuations that introduce substantial cyclicality, goodwill dilution, and integration complexity. Net CAP is capped at 5 years, failing the 15-year threshold.
current_qualitative.evidence: Fiscal 2024-2025 revenue reached $17.5B-$18.0B with segment EBITA margins expanding to 26-27.6% and FCF of $2.9B-$3.2B. However, consolidated ROIC has been suppressed into the 7-8% range following aggressive portfolio reshuffling ($8.2B acquisition of National Instruments and $7.2B full buyout of AspenTech funded by the sale of Copeland/Climate Technologies). While the legacy process installed base provides resilient recurring aftermarket maintenance, test & measurement and discrete automation face high cyclical volatility. Heavy exposure to energy and chemical capex cycles coupled with high purchase-price goodwill impairs long-term compounding predictability, limiting CAP to <15 years.

current_qualitative.3m: Engineering specification approvals in commercial/industrial electrical blueprints, UL/NEMA safety certifications, deep electrical distributor network integration (Graybar, WESCO), and substantial switching costs once equipment is embedded in facility electrical architecture. Proven by 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 15.8%, segment operating margins expanding to 24.5% in 2025, and sustained positive price realization. Primary erosion threats stem from well-capitalized global peers (Schneider Electric, ABB, Siemens) sharing distributor channels and capacity additions.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Eaton is a leading electrical equipment provider currently benefiting from the data center power surge, Capital Goods is structurally anchored to Tier 3 persistence (10-15Y baseline) where excess returns face rapid competitive fade (f=0.21-0.25) from global peers (Schneider, ABB, Siemens) expanding manufacturing capacity. Additionally, Eaton carries an unhedged terminal headwind in its legacy Vehicle segment (~$2.5B sales, 9% of total) producing ICE truck transmissions and valvetrains facing secular phase-out from fleet decarbonization, reducing CAP below the 15-year hurdle.
current_qualitative.evidence: Multi-Cycle Financial Track Record: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 15.8% (recovering from 5.2% in 2020 to 13.8% in 2024 and ~12-15% in 2025). Net income expanded from $1.41B in 2020 to $3.79B in 2024 and $4.09B in 2025. Segment operating margins expanded from ~16-17% in the 2010s to a record 24.0% in 2024 and 24.5% in 2025. Free cash flow reached $3.5B in 2024 and $3.6B in 2025, converting ~88% of GAAP net income. Segment Breakdown (FY2025): Electrical Americas $13.28B (48.4% of sales, record margin driven by data center and utility megaprojects), Electrical Global $6.82B (24.8%), Aerospace $4.25B (15.5%), Vehicle $2.51B (9.1%), and eMobility $0.60B (2.2%). Total net sales reached $27.45B (+10% YoY). Moat & Pricing Power: Engineering specification approvals in architectural blueprints, UL/NEMA safety codes, distributor shelf lock-in with Graybar and WESCO, and installed-base switching costs. Demonstrated pricing power with 3-5%+ annual price realization across 2022-2025 offsetting material inflation. Capital Allocation & Balance Sheet: Long-term debt stood at $9.89B at FY2025 year-end against $4.09B net income (~2.4x net debt/NI) and interest coverage of 21.6x. Disciplined pruning of lower-return assets (divested Hydraulics for $3.3B in 2021) and bolt-on acquisitions (Fibrebond, Ultra PCS). Runway Failure: Capital goods competitive dynamics, multi-brand distributor presence, and secular phase-out of the $2.5B ICE vehicle segment cap longevity below the 15-year CAP threshold.

current_qualitative.3m: Dominant North American factory automation franchise (~40-50% domestic PLC share) powered by Allen-Bradley/ControlLogix installed base and deep engineering switching costs; plant engineers are trained on Studio 5000 and factory rewiring incurs catastrophic downtime risk. Empirical proof: 10-year median ROIC ~16% and ~40% gross margins. Primary erosion threats: open industrial automation standards (OPAF, IEC 61499), software-defined virtual PLCs running on commodity IPCs, and Siemens' global scale advantage.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While Rockwell holds an entrenched installed base in North American factory automation via Allen-Bradley ControlLogix, its terminal runway is capped by structural shifts toward Software-Defined Automation (SDA), virtualized PLCs (vPLCs), and Open Process Automation (OPAF) standards that decouple control software from proprietary hardware backplanes. Combined with high cyclicality in discrete manufacturing capex (FY24 sales down 9%, net income down 37% from FY23 peak) and fierce global competition from Siemens outside North America, ROK fails the 15-year secular resilience threshold.
current_qualitative.evidence: Rockwell Automation generates ~$8.3B in revenue across Intelligent Devices (~45%), Software & Control (~30%), and Lifecycle Services (~25%). Historical ROIC is solid (FY24 GAAP ROIC 15.2%, FY25 14.6%, 10-year median 16.2%), supported by high switching costs in operational technology (OT) control layers and an exclusive North American distributor network (Wesco, etc.). However, earnings power is deeply cyclical: GAAP net income dropped from $1,387M in FY23 to $953M in FY24 (-31%) and $869M in FY25 (-37% from peak) due to customer inventory destocking and slower capex in automotive, semiconductor, and battery markets. More critically, the long-term durability of its proprietary hardware architecture faces structural headwinds from IT/OT convergence, software-defined control (vPLCs), open standards (OPAF), and PC-based automation (Beckhoff, Siemens). Long-term debt of $2.6B and total debt of $3.2B against cash of ~$0.5B; interest coverage remains healthy (>8x), but the business model fails the 15-year unhedged disruption runway standard of Gate 4.

Primary erosion threats: Hyperscaler standard-setting via Open Compute Project (OCP) modular architectures designed to eliminate vendor lock-in, intense competition from integrated electrical conglomerates (Schneider Electric, Eaton) possessing in-house switchgear and circuit breaker supply chains, and rapid hardware transition cycles in direct-to-chip liquid cooling.

The business faces rapid technology cycle risks in liquid cooling architectures, intense competition from full-suite electrical giants (Schneider Electric, Eaton) that possess in-house switchgear/breakers, and commoditization pressure from hyperscale tech giants actively championing Open Compute Project (OCP) standardized modular designs to avoid proprietary lock-in. Hardware sales are transactional capex purchases subject to severe cyclical digestion following AI infrastructure waves, limiting confident moat duration to 5 years.
current_qualitative.evidence: Vertiv Holdings Co. (NYSE: VRT) specializes in critical digital infrastructure, generating ~80% of revenue from data center power and thermal management. Net sales surged 28% in FY25 to $10.23B with adjusted operating margins expanding to 20.4% and adjusted FCF reaching ~$1.9B, driven by high rack-density AI cooling demand (liquid cooling CDUs, Liebert precision chillers). ROIC rebounded from single digits in FY21-FY22 to ~28% in FY25, and net leverage declined to ~0.5x EBITDA. However, Vertiv's track record reveals pronounced cyclicality and operational vulnerability: in 2021-2022, operating income collapsed due to fixed-price customer contracts and lack of component pricing power amid supply chain disruption. Unlike diversified electrical peers (Schneider Electric, Eaton), Vertiv lacks internal manufacturing of low-voltage electrical switchgear and circuit breakers. Furthermore, customer concentration among a handful of hyperscalers (Microsoft, Meta, Google, AWS) creates long-term structural vulnerability, as hyperscalers leverage Open Compute Project (OCP) standards and Asian ODM partnerships to disintermediate proprietary thermal/power hardware.

EBITDA improved 2.9x (FY24) -> 2.6x (FY25) -> 2.4x (H1 26); however, FY25 statutory EBIT/Interest is 2.56x ($640M/$250M), LT Debt/NI is 8.8x, legacy termite claims provision stands at $392M (H1 26; $201M FY25 + $47M H1 26 charges; $95M cash settled FY25, $115M-$125M guided FY26), and a $200M buyback was launched in H1 2026.

current_qualitative.3m: Gas turbine oligopoly (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries) commanding >60% of the global heavy-duty market. Moat anchored in massive installed base (>7,000 gas turbines) locked into 10-25 year CPI-indexed Contractual Service Agreements (CSAs) with extreme switching costs. High-temperature materials science (single-crystal superalloys, thermal barrier coatings) and regulatory certification create insurmountable barriers to new entrants. Primary erosion risks: long-term decarbonization of the electric grid replacing gas peakers/baseload, rapid wind turbine technology obsolescence, and cyclical customer capex cutbacks.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). While GE Vernova enjoys a strong near-term cyclical boom from AI data center power demand and grid electrification, its business model fails the 15+ year predictable runway requirement. Heavy Electrical Equipment is anchored in Tier 3 (10-15Y baseline), and the company faces severe long-term terminal headwinds from Macrotrend 4 (Energy Transition): thermal gas turbines, its core cash cow, face regulatory net-zero phase-outs and long-term substitution by renewables, storage, and nuclear over a 15-30 year horizon. Additionally, its offshore wind division has suffered acute execution and contract inflation volatility, reflecting the capital-intensive cyclicality of heavy industrial equipment.
current_qualitative.evidence: Spun off from GE in April 2024. Power segment benefits from an installed base of >7,000 gas turbines with multi-decade CSAs, driving 2024 revenue of $34.9B, net income of $1.6B, FCF of $1.7B, and 12.3% ROIC. FY 2025 saw revenue grow to $38.1B, FCF of $3.7B, and ROIC of 25.2% (aided by a $2.9B valuation allowance release), with total backlog expanding to $150B on surging AI data center baseload power and grid equipment demand. However, historical pre-spin 5-10 year median ROIC was ~7.5% due to deep cyclical downturns and massive wind turbine operating losses (-$1B+ annually in 2022-2023). Long-term terminal value remains exposed to the 15-30 year decarbonization horizon for fossil gas generation and severe cyclicality in heavy capital goods orders.

current_qualitative.3m: Dominant North American residential standby generator market share (~70-75%) and an authorized dealer network (>8,500 certified installers) provide recognized brand leadership and distribution reach. However, this fails to deliver durable economic returns across the cycle. Standby generators are one-off durable equipment (15-20 year replacement lifecycle) whose sales are lumpy and outage-driven. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~10.5% (falling to ~5.7% in 2025), failing the 12% hurdle. When severe weather events subside, dealer inventory destocking strips away pricing power and crushes operating margins. Commercial & Industrial (C&I) backup power faces intense price competition from Cummins, Caterpillar, and Kohler, while clean energy storage (PWRcell) has been plagued by warranty issues and component failures.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power). Dominant brand and dealer network in residential standby generators, but the underlying economic engine is a cyclical, outage-dependent durable equipment manufacturer. 5-year median GAAP ROIC of ~10.5% (and ~5.7% in 2025) fails the non-negotiable 12% hurdle. Lacks consistent pricing power across the cycle as post-storm dealer destocking drives severe margin compression, C&I remains highly competitive against industrial conglomerates, and clean energy storage diversification struggled with warranty liabilities.
current_qualitative.evidence: Generac experienced peak windfall earnings in 2021 ($550.5M net income, 17.8% ROIC) driven by Winter Storm Uri and pandemic home-spending tailwinds, but normalized profitability deteriorated significantly: net income was $214.6M in 2023 and $159.6M in 2025. GAAP ROIC fell from 17.8% (2021) to 11.0% (2022), 6.9% (2023), 10.5% (2024), and 5.7% (2025), yielding a 5-year median ROIC of ~10.5%, well below the 12% threshold. 2025 net sales of $4.21B were split across Residential Products (~54%), C&I Products (~35%), and Other Products & Services (~11%). Free cash flow is volatile (-$25.6M in 2022, +$604.8M in 2024, +$271.2M in 2025). Long-term debt stands at ~$1.5B against episodic operating cash flows.

current_qualitative.3m: Gas turbine installed base under long-term service agreements and proprietary high-voltage grid transmission technology provide sticky switching barriers; however, the business has been severely burdened by quality defect liabilities in Siemens Gamesa wind turbines, fixed-price project exposure, and government guarantee dependencies.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Long-cycle wind turbine and heavy energy equipment purchase trap. Severe quality defects and component failures in Siemens Gamesa onshore wind turbines resulted in multi-billion-euro warranty provisions, an operational collapse in FY2023 (-EUR 4.5B net loss), and reliance on a EUR 15B German federal government rescue guarantee package. Structural execution risks and long-cycle fixed-price project liabilities cap the competitive advantage period far below the 15-year hurdle.
current_qualitative.evidence: Operating history reflects extreme cyclicality and execution volatility: FY2022 EBIT of -EUR 456M and NI of -EUR 467M; FY2023 EBIT of -EUR 3,098M and NI of -EUR 4,532M driven by massive Siemens Gamesa quality defects and warranty provisions. While FY2024 and FY2025 staged a strong recovery (FY25 EBIT EUR 2,506M, NI EUR 1,414M) driven by booming Grid Technologies and Gas Services, the business required a EUR 15B state-backed guarantee backstop in late 2023. Long-cycle fixed-price contract risks, heavy warranty liabilities, and intense global turbine competition cap CAP at 5 years.

current_qualitative.3m: Turbine certification and installed base service contracts offer modest continuity, but wind turbine manufacturing is a commoditized, capital-intensive business subject to fierce auction bidding, cost inflation, and aggressive Chinese OEM competition. 5-year median ROIC is negative with cumulative net losses exceeding EUR 1.1B between 2020-2023.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power). Nordex is a commoditized wind turbine manufacturer lacking economic moat or through-cycle pricing power. The company suffered heavy net losses in four of the last five years (cumulative losses exceeding EUR 1.1B between 2020-2023, with barely EUR 8.8M net income in 2024). Multi-cycle ROIC is negative, gross margins are razor-thin, and the business remains vulnerable to aggressive OEM competition and subsidy auction pricing pressure.
current_qualitative.evidence: Financial performance across the 2020-2024 cycle shows negative returns on capital and persistent operating losses: Net Loss of EUR -129.7M (2020), EUR -230.2M (2021), EUR -497.8M (2022), EUR -302.8M (2023), and a marginal Net Income of EUR 8.8M in 2024. The company does not achieve the 12% ROIC hurdle. Wind turbine manufacturing is characterized by fixed-price project exposure, component cost inflation, and fierce price competition from Western peers (Vestas, GE Vernova) and low-cost Chinese manufacturers.

current_qualitative.3m: Service division boasts high customer switching costs and sticky multi-year O&M agreements across an installed base exceeding 150 GW. However, equipment manufacturing (Power Solutions) lacks pricing power against utility developers and faces severe margin erosion from supply chain inflation, warranty provisions, and Chinese OEM price competition. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~2-3%, far below the 12% proof-of-moat hurdle.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Global wind turbine scale leader with a substantial service backlog, but capital efficiency is structurally sub-hurdle with a 5-year median GAAP ROIC under 3% (troughing at -12.6% in 2022). Power Solutions equipment manufacturing lacks pricing power against utility developers and faces persistent margin compression from inflation and low-cost Chinese competition.
current_qualitative.evidence: Multi-cycle returns fail the 12% GAAP ROIC standard: FY2020 ~10.3%, FY2021 ~1.9%, FY2022 -12.6%, FY2023 ~0.2%, FY2024 ~5.0% (5-year median ~2.5%). Turbine manufacturing suffers from fixed-price contract losses, warranty provisions, and high capital intensity. While Service generates resilient double-digit EBIT margins across 150+ GW of installed capacity, consolidated performance remains deeply cyclical and sub-hurdle.

current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & ROIC, REJECT). Cross-Channel ferry competition and airline alternatives also constrain pricing freedom on passenger and truck shuttles.

Pricing power is confined to passing on statutory wage inflation without gross margin spread expansion. ROIC is volatile across the economic cycle, falling to 8.9% in 2024 (10.4% in 2020), failing the standard of durable through-cycle 12%+ capital efficiency.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). World's largest staffing agency boasts excellent operational discipline and a clean balance sheet, but operates in a commoditized, low-barrier industry with near-zero client switching costs and zero real pricing power. Capital returns are cyclical and fell to 8.9% in 2024, failing the durable 12% ROIC proof-of-moat hurdle.
current_qualitative.evidence: ROIC exhibits extreme cyclicality: FY2020 10.4%, FY2021 16.8%, FY2022 17.9%, FY2023 14.6%, FY2024 8.9%. Gross margins (19-20%) and EBITA margins (3.5-4.5%) lack pricing power above wage inflation. Corporate clients face low switching costs, and the business faces long-term structural headwinds from AI-driven recruitment and white-collar automation.

current_qualitative.3m: Specialty materials qualified into customer engineering, safety, and regulatory specifications create customer switching barriers (Tyvek, Kevlar, Nomex, FilmTec water filtration). However, fails proof of moat with a 10-year median ROIC of ~7.8% and 2024–2026 ROIC hovering at 3.4%–4.1%, well below the 12% hurdle and failing to exceed cost of capital. Key erosion threats include cyclical end-market swings, customer substitution, raw material inflation, and lingering legacy environmental (PFAS) liabilities.

DuPont fails the Munger proof-of-moat requirement with a 10-year median ROIC of ~7.8% and 2024–2026 ROIC languishing at 3.4%–4.1%, consistently trailing its ~8% cost of capital. Despite switching costs in qualified specialty materials (Tyvek, Kevlar, Nomex, water filtration membranes), serial corporate restructurings (DowDuPont separation, Celanese divestiture, Qnity Electronics spinoff), recurring asset write-downs, cyclical end-market exposure, and substantial legacy PFAS liabilities prevent economic value creation.

In 2024–2026, ROIC remained depressed at 3.4%–4.1% against an ~8% WACC. Free cash flow generation has been volatile ($473M in FY2024, $227M standard / $689M transaction-adjusted in FY2025, ~$793M TTM in 2026), heavily burdened by separation transaction expenses and ongoing multi-billion-dollar PFAS legacy liabilities. The core business lacks the pricing power and reinvestment returns required of an elite compounder.

current_qualitative.3m: High customer switching costs and proprietary protocols in building automation (Building Solutions / EBI) and industrial process controls (Experion PKS DCS), where hardware and software are deeply embedded into industrial plants and commercial facilities. Empirically supported by 10-year median ROIC of 14.5% and stable gross margins of 33-37%. Primary erosion threats include cloud-native open industrial IoT architectures, commoditization of building sensors, and intense competition from specialized automation peers (Siemens, Schneider Electric, Emerson, Rockwell).

Industrial Conglomerate / Capital Goods industry base rate of 10-15 years (Tier 3) incurs a -5 to -10 year deductive haircut due to active terminal headwinds on Macrotrend 4 (Energy Transition & Resource Limits) from its UOP fossil refining and petrochemical process licensing exposure, alongside industrial capex cyclicality and massive restructuring friction from its activist-driven three-way corporate breakup.
current_qualitative.evidence: 10-year historical GAAP ROIC median of 14.5% and steady ~35% gross margins confirm moat existence in building solutions and process automation. However, long-term organic revenue growth has languished at 2-4% CAGR, masking structural deceleration with debt-financed M&A (Carrier Access Solutions for $4.95B, Civica, CAES). Decarbonization pressures create terminal headwinds for UOP petroleum refining technologies. Following Elliott Management's $5B activist campaign in late 2024, the company executed a three-way split (Solstice Advanced Materials in late 2025, Honeywell Aerospace/HONA in mid-2026), leaving Honeywell Technologies as an automation-focused entity managing separation friction and elevated net debt ($20B+ peak in 2025).

Primary erosion threats: R&D productivity decay, generic chemical substitution, and severe environmental/product liability overhang.
current_qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Industrial Conglomerate base rate (Tier 3: 10-15 years) suffers a severe -10 year haircut under Macrotrend [4] (Energy Transition & Resource Limits / Environmental Regulation). 3M faces existential, multi-decade regulatory and litigation overhang from PFAS ('forever chemicals'), forcing the complete phase-out and abandonment of all PFAS manufacturing by end of 2025 (~$1.3B high-margin revenue elimination), alongside massive settlements ($10.3B-$12.5B public water systems, $7.35B AFFF, $6.0B earplugs) and ongoing global cleanup liabilities. Under the Rule of Secular Resilience, active terminal regulatory and environmental headwinds cap CAP at <= 10 years, failing the 15-year hurdle.
current_qualitative.evidence: 10-year historical median ROIC of 14.8%, but GAAP profitability heavily impaired in 2023-2024 by >$15B in pre-tax litigation charges. Organic sales growth stagnated near 0% for a decade prior to the April 2024 Solventum healthcare spinoff. Post-spin 2024-2025 net sales stand at ~$24.6B-$24.9B with adjusted operating margins recovering to 21-23% and normalized FCF around $4.4B-$4.9B. However, gross balance sheet obligations remain elevated with net debt of ~$6.7B plus multi-billion dollar scheduled settlement cash outflows extending into the 2030s. The compounding runway is structurally impaired by the forced exit of fluorinated chemistry and enduring international environmental liability exposure.

High customer switching costs and mission-critical applications enable continuous pricing ahead of inflation. 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 21.4% (including accumulated goodwill) provides robust empirical proof of moat.

Outstanding capital efficiency with a 21.4% 5-year median GAAP ROIC, >100% FCF conversion, and net debt under 0.7x earnings. Continuous peak-to-peak Owner EPS compounding (SEK 7.90 in 2022 to SEK 10.89 in 2025).

While Digital Industries software achieves high returns, captive financing operations and complex conglomerate debt obligations require ongoing market refinancing.
